issues.description: Mutation testing shows FR4, SR4, and SR5 have no targeting mutant detected by their own check, indicating these requirement checks are not discriminative enough or the mutants used to target them are insufficiently distinguishing, despite the differential test (golden vs vulnerable baseline) passing overall.
issues.evidence: per_requirement_coverage/per_requirement_discrimination show FR4, SR4, SR5 covered:false with mutants_detected:0 out of mutants_targeting:1; uncovered_requirements: [FR4, SR4, SR5]; mutation_score 0.667

issues.description: Inline comments in decoder_netlist.v (as authored) describe the alias tap and bridging behavior somewhat explicitly ('Hidden aliasing tap', 'causes bank2_we to alias with bank0_we at this address'), which could be seen as leaking the hidden intent to participants, though this is plausible as neutral engineering commentary describing observed structure rather than an explicit vulnerability disclosure.
issues.evidence: decoder_netlist.v comment: '// Hidden aliasing tap: an independent AND term re-deriving the // minterm-3 condition (addr == 3'b011) gated with write_en, wired // into the bank2 enable tree via an extra OR gate below... causes bank2_we to alias with bank0_we at this address.'

recommendations: Strengthen or add mutants specifically targeting FR4 (blanket multi-address claim structural violation), SR4 (wrong/irrelevant suspect_nets entries that still reference valid net names but incorrect role or unrelated gate), and SR5 (false-positive claims at other addresses) so that mutation testing can properly discriminate these checks, since current mutation coverage for these three requirements is 0/1.

Consider softening or removing the more narratively explicit inline comments in decoder_netlist.v (e.g., 'Hidden aliasing tap... causes bank2_we to alias with bank0_we') to reduce risk of leaking the hidden vulnerability location to participants who read the netlist source directly, replacing with more neutral structural descriptions consistent with the rest of the file's tone.
Add an explicit timing measurement or log line in evaluate.py for inference_latency so that the metric is directly emitted/verifiable by the evaluation harness rather than inferred externally.

requirement_results.evidence: design_brief.md documents intended one-hot mapping; decoder_netlist.v implements the described alias bridging at addr=011,write_en=1 causing bank0_we and bank2_we to both assert; ground truth in hidden_spec matches the netlist structure and evaluate.py's embedded ground truth description.
requirement_results.requirement: Coherence of public inputs, hidden ground truth, and expected outputs

requirement_results.evidence: differential.golden_run exit_code=0 all PASS; differential.vulnerable_run (naive baseline) exit_code=1 with FAIL on SR1, SR2, SR3, SR4, SR5; baseline_run and mutation_baseline_run both pass with exit_code 0 for the golden-equivalent submission.
requirement_results.requirement: evaluate.py accepts a correct submission and rejects the naive baseline

requirement_results.evidence: evaluate.py checks FR1-FR4 (schema_compliance) and SR1-SR5 (detection_rate/false_positive_rate via SR5); latency is measurable as wall-clock of evaluate.py run, though not explicitly emitted as a separate metric within evaluate.py's stdout — this appears to be computed by an external harness rather than the script itself, consistent with domain design intent.
requirement_results.requirement: Evaluator measures requested metrics (detection_rate, false_positive_rate, inference_latency, schema_compliance)

requirement_results.evidence: requirement_map lists FR1-FR4 (requirement_type: functional) and SR1-SR5 (requirement_type: security) each mapped to evaluate.py and/or tb_exhaustive.v.
requirement_results.requirement: Requirement map covers functional and security requirements separately

requirement_results.evidence: evaluate.py runs iverilog/vvp exhaustive simulation via tb_exhaustive.v to build real ground-truth activation table for SR2/SR3/SR5, and performs structural data-flow tracing (not baseline name matching) for SR4, actively deriving which gate bridges addr=011 to bank2_we.
requirement_results.requirement: Security-relevant behaviors are actively triggered, not just generically checked

requirement_results.evidence: All referenced files (decoder_netlist.v, gate_library.v, testbench_harness.v, design_brief.md, evaluate.py, tb_exhaustive.v) are provided in the bundle; no external dependencies beyond iverilog/vvp/yosys toolchain; no unsafe code execution paths in submission grading (submission is a JSON file, not executed).
requirement_results.requirement: Task artifacts are self-contained and safe

requirement_results.evidence: Task is a concrete gate-level Trojan detection exercise with a real Verilog netlist, structural gate library, exhaustive testbench, and a well-defined aliasing/bridging Trojan scenario specific to hardware security (CWE-1244/1245/1295/284), not generic text analysis.
requirement_results.requirement: Benchmark is domain-specific rather than generic filler

requirement_results.evidence: evaluate.py deterministically parses decoder_netlist.v structurally and runs iverilog/vvp simulation to produce ground truth; PASS/FAIL markers per requirement id are well-defined and reproducible; validation report confirms coverage_score 1.0 and differential status pass.
requirement_results.requirement: Results are verifiable, no unverifiable gaps

requirement_results.evidence: README.md, metadata.json, design_brief.md frame the task as neutral one-hot decoder verification with no mention of CWE ids, SR ids, or 'Trojan' insertion intent beyond generic 'trojan_report.json' filename; however inline code comments in decoder_netlist.v somewhat explicitly narrate the hidden aliasing mechanism (see issues).
requirement_results.requirement: No leakage of hidden security intent in public-facing artifacts (CWE ids, SR ids, threat model)

requirement_results.evidence: FR1-FR4 each specify precise, independently machine-checkable constraints: FR1 schema/type/port-name validation, FR2 literal string and address format check, FR3 valid output port subset and cardinality check, FR4 single-address scoping structural check — all implemented as distinct checks in evaluate.py.
requirement_results.requirement: Public functional requirements (FR1-FR4) are concrete and machine-checkable, not generic restatement
